entries.why: The private-use citation markers (\ue200-\ue206) and the turn{N}{type}{index} anchor grammar, in both literal and character form.
entries.failure_mode: A marker or ref type upstream adds renders as raw text after the cited sentence, or is stripped where the web shows a source chip.

entries.why: Which search-result list each anchor type indexes (search -> organic, news -> topStories, ref/file -> references).
entries.failure_mode: An anchor resolves to the wrong result list, so the pill names and opens a different source than the one the model cited.

entries.why: How a reply's web_search and file_search attachments become the per-turn results its anchors index into.
entries.failure_mode: Citations stop resolving (and are stripped), or resolve against the wrong search turn.

entries.why: How a copied message writes its citations: [n] numbered by link, highlights in bold, a Citations: footer.
entries.failure_mode: A copied reply diverges from what the web copies for the same message.

entries.why: When a web search reads as searching, processing, reading or settled, and when it falls back to the failed tool card or draws nothing.
entries.failure_mode: The card shows a phase or a settled state the web does not, e.g. a failed search drawn as a sources card.

entries.why: Which tool outputs count as a failure (error prefix, 'Error processing tool', validation feedback).
entries.failure_mode: A failed search renders as a successful one, or a successful one as failed.

entries.why: Which image, shopping and place results are drawn (the URL allowlist, required fields, the 8/8/5 caps) and the map link format.
entries.failure_mode: A result upstream drops shows as a dead tile, or one it shows is missing.

entries.why: How a file search's text output is split into sections and matched to its files by normalized name.
entries.failure_mode: File search results list in a different order, or open the wrong file, or none.

entries.why: The header of a tool group made only of web and file searches: its label and favicons.
entries.failure_mode: A group of searches reads as 'Used N tools', or a mixed group reads as searches.

entries.why: How a multi-agent reply's search results split into the All / News / Images / Files tabs, and how many cards show before '+N'.
entries.failure_mode: The Compare sources panel lists results under the wrong tab or misses some.

entries.why: The web_search tool's text output is built by formatResultsForLLM in the @librechat/agents npm package (src/tools/search/format.ts), not in this repo, so the closest watch is the package pin. A Stop after the search persists that output but not the web_search attachment, and the card lists the sources by parsing its '# Search N: "title"' blocks and their URL / Summary / Date / Source lines. Checked identical at 3.2.01 and 3.4.7. When this reports DRIFT, look only at the @librechat/agents version; if it moved, diff dist/esm/tools/search/format.mjs between the two versions (unpkg) and dismiss if formatSource is unchanged.
entries.failure_mode: A stopped search's card shows 'Searched the web' with no sources, as upstream's web does. Nothing errors.

entries.why: An `iconURL` (a spec's, a preset's, a conversation's, an endpoint's) is either an image or the name of an endpoint or provider whose glyph to borrow. Web decides which with `isImageURL`: an absolute or protocol-relative URL, a `data:image/` URI, a rooted path, or a bare file name with an image extension. The picker, landing, Compare and the conversation rows decide the same way.
entries.failure_mode: If web accepts another image form, mobile draws a generic glyph where web draws the admin's image; if it narrows, mobile tries to load a name as a URL and falls back to the glyph. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: A spec's icon is its own `iconURL`, then its preset's, then its agent's avatar (agent specs only), then its endpoint's name, skipping empty strings. The picker rows, the landing hero and Compare's spec lane all take it from here.
entries.failure_mode: If web reorders the chain or adds a source, the same spec shows a different icon on mobile than on web.

entries.why: Which brand art an endpoint, spec or conversation row draws: an image `iconURL`, then an `iconURL` naming a provider (`groq`, `grok`), then the endpoint's served `providerId` (the server derives it from the custom endpoint's `baseURL` host, which the client never sees), then the first-class endpoint's brand, then the endpoint's own name.
entries.failure_mode: If web reorders the rules or adds one, the same endpoint draws different art on mobile than on web; nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The `ProviderId` wire ids the server serves as `EndpointConfig.providerId`, which `resolveProviderId` matches by normalised id.
entries.failure_mode: A new provider id upstream decodes fine (`providerId` is a String) and just draws the generic glyph on mobile.

entries.why: Which first-class endpoint draws which provider's brand.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream remaps or adds a first-class endpoint, and mobile draws the old brand or the generic glyph where web draws the new one.

entries.why: The alias table that turns a free-form name or `iconURL` (`claude`, `vertexai`, `mistralai`) into a provider. `knownEndpointToProvider` isn't ported: normalisation and the aliases cover its keys.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds an alias, and an endpoint or spec named by it draws the generic glyph on mobile where web draws the brand.

entries.why: How a name is normalised before the id and alias lookups: lowercased, with spaces, dots, underscores and hyphens stripped.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream strips or keeps another separator, and a name web resolves to a brand draws the generic glyph on mobile, or the reverse.

entries.why: The lookup order: the normalised id first, then the aliases.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds a step (a prefix match, a third table), and mobile resolves fewer names to a brand than web.

entries.why: The names web gives endpoint keys (`anthropic` reads "Anthropic"), used by `endpointDisplayName` after an endpoint's `modelDisplayLabel` for picker headers, Compare's quick-pick source, the missing-key send block and error, and the provider keys list. `agents` and `custom` are left out: those screens have translated strings.
entries.failure_mode: A key upstream starts naming shows its raw key on mobile, such as `anthropic` in lowercase.

entries.why: Which providers have art on the user's server and its file name (`providerAssetFiles`, loaded from `{server}/assets/<file>`), and each provider's `label` (`ProviderId.label`, the content description). No logo art is bundled in the app. Since v0.8.9-rc1 web draws every provider as an inline mark and references none of these files; they are the legacy files `client/public/assets/` still ships, each watched by its own `provider-asset-*` entry.
