entries.why: How a conversation row picks its icon: an image `iconURL` wins; a non-image `iconURL` switches the icon endpoint only when it is an endpoints-config key (`getIconEndpoint`, `icon-endpoint-rule`); the provider art is then resolved for that endpoint without the conversation's own `iconURL`. The drawer's endpoint filter chips draw the same icon (`filterEndpointOption`). Web then passes `model` to `MinimalIcon` for the model-maker override, which mobile doesn't port (`provider-icon-registry`).
entries.failure_mode: Drawer, list and archive rows draw different icons than web's sidebar.

entries.why: Which endpoint's icon an `iconURL` stands for: the `iconURL` itself when the endpoints config lists it as a key, else the conversation's or message's endpoint. Conversation rows, filter chips and reply avatars all use it.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream widens the match (labels, case), and rows and replies draw a different endpoint's brand than web's.

entries.why: What a reply's avatar draws: an image `iconURL` is loaded; any other value counts only as an endpoint key (`getIconEndpoint`), and that endpoint's configured image `iconURL` is loaded, else its brand drawn, so a spec icon naming a provider (`groq`) draws the reply's endpoint, unlike the picker. An agents reply draws its agent's avatar (found by the message's `model`, else the chat's agent, as `useMessageActions` does) ahead of the endpoint's image. The streaming reply and Compare's lane B use the same rule (`ModelSpec.replyIconSource`). Web passes `model` for the model-maker override, which mobile doesn't port.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes the rule, mobile's reply avatars disagree with web's, or with the drawer row for the same chat.

entries.why: What a spec draws in the picker, the landing hero and Compare's quick picks: `agents` draws the agents mark, an image is loaded, a value naming a provider draws that brand, else the spec endpoint's brand. Mobile draws `assistants` as OpenAI, on purpose, where web draws its entity mark.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes the order (entity, image, brand), mobile's picker draws a different icon for the same spec.

entries.why: What a custom spec group's header draws for its `groupIcon`: an image is loaded, a value naming a provider draws that brand. Mobile also draws an endpoint key's served brand, which web's `GroupIcon` doesn't.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes the rule, a custom group's header draws a different icon on mobile than on web.

entries.why: What the new chat's hero draws: the selected spec's icon by the `SpecIcon` rule, else the agent's avatar, else the endpoint's configured `iconURL` (`iconURL || configured` in `useProviderIcon`), else its brand. The "+" sheet's Model cell draws the same icon.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes the precedence, mobile's landing hero draws a different icon from web's.

entries.why: Which icon values draw an entity's mark instead of a provider's (`SpecIcon`, `GroupIcon`): `agents`, `assistants` and `azureAssistants`. Mobile draws the agents mark for `agents` only; it has no Assistants endpoints.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream adds an entity endpoint, a spec or group icon naming it draws that name's brand or the generic glyph on mobile and an entity mark on web.

entries.why: An endpoint that needs the user's key gets a Set API Key button in web's `EndpointItem`, which still lists its nested specs. Mobile greys the header behind Add key, keeps the grouped specs listed (a tap opens the key screen) and hides the raw models. Mobile reads the per-endpoint key state (unset or expired) rather than the bare `userProvide` flag.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes what counts as needing a key or what it lists under such an endpoint, mobile hides specs web lists or shows models web gates.

entries.why: Web disables the composer when the selected endpoint takes a user-provided key (`userProvide`) and the user has none stored (no expiry). Mobile refuses the send in the preflight with the same rule instead of letting the server fail it with `no_user_key`; like the picker it lets the send through while the key state is loading or unknown.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes when a key counts as required (say, per spec or per agent provider), and mobile blocks sends web allows or lets through sends the server refuses.

entries.why: How the picker places a spec by its `group`: none at the top, a group exactly equal to a shown endpoint's key at the top of that endpoint's section (EndpointItem.tsx), any other group a headed group after the endpoints with the first `groupIcon` found (this file). With `modelSelect: false` no endpoint is shown, so every group is a custom one. Mobile keeps its own `order` sort within each group, and puts a spec grouped under a model-less endpoint in a group of its own where web hides it.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes the matching (case, labels instead of keys) or the icon pick, mobile groups the same specs differently from web.

entries.why: A spec nests in an endpoint's section when its `group` is exactly that endpoint's key (`spec.group === endpoint.value`): not its label, and case-sensitive. `model-spec-groups` watches the custom-group half of the same rule.
entries.failure_mode: If web starts matching labels or ignoring case, a spec web nests under an endpoint shows as a group of its own on mobile.

entries.why: The new chat's title is the selected agent's name, else the spec's label when it has `showOnLanding`; its description is the agent's, then that spec's description, then the conversation's `greeting` (a spec's preset greeting). `landingText` returns these and the temporary chat's own title and subtitle whatever the flag, and `LandingContent` switches each line as temporary chat's band reaches it. A temporary chat also replaces the spec's or agent's icon with a temporary glyph, as web swaps in `HatGlasses`; mobile draws the temporary toggle's `VisibilityOff` in temporary violet instead, on purpose. Mobile renders the description as plain text (at most 4 lines, 2 in compact) where web renders sanitized markdown.
entries.failure_mode: If web changes the precedence or what `showOnLanding` controls, mobile's landing names or describes the chat differently from web's.

entries.why: Compare's second model takes its spec preset's settings only as flat `addedConvo` fields the server copies by name (`temperature`, `top_p`/`topP`, `topK`, the penalties, `maxOutputTokens`, `maxTokens`/`max_tokens`), and only when the primary is a saved agent. `AddedConversation` sends the preset's own names for them: `top_p` and `max_tokens`, not the camelCase aliases.
entries.failure_mode: If the server reads more fields or applies them for an ephemeral primary too, lane B silently runs without settings its spec sets.

entries.why: A reopened comparison's second lane gets its spec back from the sender in its saved agent id, which is `modelLabel ?? spec.label ?? modelDisplayLabel`. The server saves nothing else about that lane's spec.
entries.failure_mode: If the sender stops carrying the spec's label, a reopened comparison's second lane runs without its spec's tools and settings (or, under `enforce`, asks for a pick).

entries.why: Which reply offers Continue: the latest, with a finish_reason other than `stop` and `tool_call_limit` (Constants.TOOL_CALL_LIMIT_FINISH_REASON), never one with no user turn behind it or a compaction. Mobile also counts a reply saved `unfinished`, which is what a v0.8.8 agents stop leaves.
entries.failure_mode: If web starts offering Continue on other replies, or the server starts saving a finish_reason for stopped replies, mobile's chip shows on different replies than web's button.

entries.why: Keep this answer / Keep and continue put the server's branched message into the tree from the response, as web appends it to its cached list without refetching. A temporary chat never loads from the server or Room, so this is the only way the kept reply reaches its screen.
entries.failure_mode: If web starts refetching instead (or the route stops returning the whole saved message), mobile's merge shows a message the server no longer describes that way; in a temporary chat, Keep and continue times out with 'Failed to continue' and the old two-lane reply stays on screen.

entries.why: A Compare lane is named by each content part's `agentId`, as web groups its columns. At the end of a run the panes fill a lane id no text delta named (a lane stopped inside its first tool call) from the final message's parts, so that pane still offers Keep.
entries.failure_mode: If lanes stop being read from `part.agentId`, a lane stopped before it wrote text offers no Keep or Keep and continue until the conversation is reopened.

entries.why: The user-key members of ErrorTypes (no_user_key, expired_user_key, invalid_user_key, no_base_url, invalid_base_url): the codes a failed send carries when the fix is on the Provider Keys sheet. parseUserKeyError maps each to a UserKeyError, which routes the failure to a snackbar with a Provider Keys action instead of the generic error. The block is the whole enum, so most DRIFT reports are other members' churn: check the five user-key members, not the enum.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed or new user-key code is not recognised, so the send fails with the raw payload or generic text and no way to the sheet that fixes it. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The key collection's TTL index (expireAfterSeconds: 0 on expiresAt) deletes a user key once it expires, on MongoDB's 60-second TTL pass. Chat schedules a key-state recompute at each key's expiry and one more a TTL pass later, so the model picker locks an endpoint when its key runs out, says 'Key expired' only while the server still holds the key, and 'Needs your key' once it is gone.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream drops the TTL index or keeps keys past expiry, the picker reads an expired key as gone a minute early, or keeps saying 'Key expired' after the server has deleted it. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which endpoints the Provider Keys page lists and the Settings row counts: the reachable ones (all without model specs; else the specs' endpoints plus addedEndpoints, plus the agents' allowedProviders, or every non-agents, non-assistants endpoint when unrestricted, if the user has AGENTS USE) that take a user-provided credential (userProvide or any Bedrock per-field flag). Deliberate divergences: base-URL-only (userProvideURL) endpoints are kept, because mobile chat still needs the URL set; AGENTS USE is permissive while the role is unknown, as the app's other USE gates are; and the list is sorted by order, then label.
entries.failure_mode: The page lists an endpoint the user cannot reach, or misses one whose key their chats need. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which form each endpoint gets on the key sheet (Google, OpenAI-style, Custom, Bedrock, or the one-field default), and so which wire shape its key is saved in. Mobile mirrors web's mapping, including treating azureAssistants as plain OpenAI. Its sibling formSet (same file) decides which endpoints go through the structured-form submit path; a change to either is a change here.
entries.failure_mode: An endpoint gets the wrong form and saves its key in a shape the server does not read: the save succeeds and every chat on that endpoint then fails as if no key were set.

entries.why: Which endpoints submit through the structured form (an {apiKey, baseURL} JSON value) rather than as a raw string. It differs from endpointComponents: google has its own component but is not in this set. Mobile's form kinds encode the same split (OPENAI/CUSTOM/AZURE/BEDROCK send JSON; GOOGLE its own object; OTHER the raw key).
entries.failure_mode: An endpoint moved between the two paths upstream is saved by mobile in the other shape; the save succeeds and chats on it fail as if no key were set.

entries.why: The expiry choices offered for a new key, their durations, the 12-hour default and 'never' sent as no expiry.
entries.failure_mode: Mobile offers different expiry windows than web, or a duration that no longer matches its label. Nothing errors.

entries.why: submit()'s required-field rules and wire shapes: baseURL optional for OpenAI-base endpoints and required for a custom endpoint with userProvideURL, Azure's quad stringified into apiKey, and Bedrock's rules (only flagged fields count, trimmed; a bearer token alone is complete and sent on its own; otherwise every flagged access-key field is required, the bearer token too when it is the only credential offered) with the credentials stringified into apiKey beside an empty baseURL. Deliberate divergences: a Bedrock endpoint whose config carries none of the per-field flags (a server older than them) keeps the flat {accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?} with the session token optional; and an OpenAI-base endpoint with userProvideURL but not userProvide (base URL only) asks for and requires the base URL alone, sending apiKey as "", because packages/api's openai initialize reads the key from the server's environment then and only baseURL from the stored value (web demands a key the server ignores). A custom endpoint still requires the key there: its initialize reads the user's apiKey whenever it reads any user value.
entries.failure_mode: A rule or shape change upstream makes mobile refuse a key the server would take, or save one in a shape the server no longer reads, which surfaces later as a chat failing with no_user_key or a credentials error.

entries.why: What counts as a Google service-account key: client_email a valid email (zod 3's email pattern, copied) of at least 3 characters, project_id at least 3, private_key at least 601. Mobile applies it to a pasted key as well as an imported file, and refuses to save a key that fails it.
entries.failure_mode: A schema change upstream makes mobile refuse a key web accepts, or save one web would reject and the server then fails to use.

entries.why: One Bedrock field per credential the endpoint config flags as user-provided (userProvideAccessKeyId, userProvideSecretAccessKey, userProvideSessionToken, userProvideBearerToken). Web lists the bearer token last; the app puts it first, since on its own it is the whole credential.
entries.failure_mode: A credential upstream adds or renames is never asked for, so a Bedrock key saved from mobile is missing it and Bedrock chats fail with a credentials error.

entries.why: The reserved tag name behind the favorite star and the drawer's Favorites section, hidden from every bookmark list and refused as a bookmark name. `SAVED_TAG` is one member of the large `Constants` enum, so most changes to this block are unrelated; check only that member.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream renames it, favorites written on mobile stop matching the tag web treats as Saved, and a bookmark of the old name turns into the star. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The longest bookmark title the editor accepts (web's title `maxLength`, 128). Client-side only: the server stores any length.
entries.failure_mode: Mobile accepts titles web would refuse, or refuses ones web accepts. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The longest bookmark description the editor accepts (web's description `maxLength`, 1048). Client-side only: the server stores any length.
entries.failure_mode: Mobile accepts descriptions web would refuse, or refuses ones web accepts. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The edit and delete routes run `decodeURIComponent` on a tag param Express has already decoded, so the client escapes the name twice. Check that the extra decode is still there.
entries.failure_mode: If upstream drops the extra decode, a name with `%` or an escaped character is edited or deleted under the wrong spelling: a 404, or the wrong bookmark. Plain names keep working, so it goes unnoticed.

entries.why: Bookmark reordering copies three behaviours of this file. `adjustPositions` shifts the tags between a moved tag's old and new stored position by one (`shiftPositions`, and `spreadPositions` which un-ties positions with it), so `reorderTag` sends the stored position of the tag in the target slot, not an index. `updateTagsForConversation` files a name it hasn't seen at position 0, so `writeChatTag` posts every name it attaches through `POST /api/tags` first, without checking the cached list (which can be stale). That relies on `createConversationTag` returning an existing name early, unchanged and without error; it also skips the attach for it, so `createTag` attaches through the chat PUT.
entries.failure_mode: If the shift or the position semantics change (e.g. to the index web sends), a drag lands in the wrong slot after the refresh. If the chat PUT or the create changes, new bookmarks land first in the order, or one isn't added to the chat; if the create starts refusing an existing name, every tick fails. Nothing else errors.

entries.why: The native client captures and carries the OpenID provider and signed user marker; the user marker binds to the refresh-token hash and must rotate with it.
entries.failure_mode: A changed cookie name, marker lifetime or binding rule silently breaks OpenID reuse while normal logins still work.

entries.why: Native refresh carries the server-issued cookie bundle and retains omitted response cookies. OpenID reuse is selected by token_provider, not the sign-in provider label.
entries.failure_mode: A changed refresh-routing or cookie-rotation contract rejects native sessions after login or refresh.

entries.why: The non-OpenID refresh refreshController hands off to since v0.8.9-rc1: which arms clear the refreshToken cookie (a retired token's 401, the TWO_FACTOR_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED 200 that carries no token) and which rotate it. CookieHelper.update reads a cleared refreshToken as a dead session, so the enrollment arm has to be told apart before it.
entries.failure_mode: A changed refresh-routing or cookie-rotation contract rejects native sessions after login or refresh. An arm that newly clears the cookie on a 200 lands the session in refresh limbo instead of re-auth.

entries.why: An IdP bearer requires both OpenID marker cookies on authenticated API and SSE requests; iOS raw SSE mirrors the same contract.
entries.failure_mode: Login succeeds but subsequent native bearer requests fail authentication because a new strategy-selection rule was not mirrored.

kotlin.symbol: Preset (and Conversation, ConversationParameters.kt, AddedConversation: one field per spelling)

entries.why: Upstream spells Top P and max output tokens per provider (`top_p` / `max_tokens` for openAI, azure and custom; `topP` for google, anthropic and bedrock; `maxOutputTokens` for google and anthropic; `maxTokens` for bedrock), and each endpoint schema keeps only its own spelling. Preset and Conversation hold one field per spelling (`topPSnake` / `topPCamel`, `maxTokensSnake` / `maxTokensCamel`, `maxOutputTokens`), and `mergedFromPreset` coalesces them into one slot. A key upstream adds or respells has no field here, so nothing reads it.
entries.failure_mode: A conversation or spec carrying the new key reopens without it, mobile sends the default, and the server unsets the stored value on the first send (getUnsetFields), erasing what web set.

entries.why: The keys the server keeps for openAI, azure and custom endpoints (it parses custom with openAISchema). The registry's openAI list must spell each value the way this schema picks it, or the server strips it.
entries.failure_mode: A control is offered and its value sent under a key the schema strips: the setting does nothing, and the stored value under the right key is unset.

entries.why: The keys the server keeps for the anthropic endpoint. The registry's Anthropic list must spell each value the way this schema picks it.
entries.failure_mode: A value sent under a key the schema strips does nothing, and the stored value is unset.

entries.why: The keys the server keeps for the google endpoint. The registry's Google list must spell each value the way this schema picks it.
entries.failure_mode: A value sent under a key the schema strips does nothing, and the stored value is unset.

entries.why: Which parameter set a custom endpoint uses: `customParams.defaultParamsEndpoint` (the server fills it from the endpoint's `provider`), else its `type`. Web's Panel.tsx and the agent model panel resolve it the same way. The registry is keyed on the result, never on the endpoint's own name, which names no parameter set.
entries.failure_mode: A custom endpoint falls back to the generic list: its Top P and max tokens go out camelCased and the server's openAISchema strips them, along with every OpenAI-only control.

entries.why: The server honours `customParams.defaultParamsEndpoint` only when it is exactly one of these keys (`isEndpointSchemaLookupKey`); any other value parses with the endpoint `type`'s schema. `paramSettingsKey` accepts the override on the same test.
entries.failure_mode: An override the server ignores (or one it newly accepts) picks a different parameter set on the client: values go out under keys the server's schema strips, and the stored values are unset.

kotlin.symbol: bedrockAnthropic / bedrockMistral / bedrockCohere / bedrockGeneral / bedrockMoonshot / bedrockZai

entries.why: The keys Bedrock knows. Any other key is moved into `additionalModelRequestFields` and sent to AWS, so the Bedrock variant lists hold only what upstream lists. Claude effort is `effort` (sent as `output_config.effort`); the parser deletes `reasoning_effort` for Claude.
entries.failure_mode: A control sends a key the parser forwards to AWS (which may reject the request) or deletes (the control does nothing).

entries.why: The fields a Bedrock conversation stores, for every model: it keeps `stop`, `maxTokens` and `topK` though web's panels show them only for some variants. A spec preset or a reopened chat still carries them, and the server unsets any stored field a request omits, so `wireOnlyDefinitions` sends the ones a variant's list leaves out.
entries.failure_mode: If the schema drops a key, mobile sends a field the server discards. If it adds one a panel hides, a spec's value for it is erased on the next mobile send.

entries.why: Every chat turn unsets each stored conversation field the request leaves out (except `excludedKeys`). The payload sends only registry keys, so a key the client drops or misspells is erased from the conversation, including one set on web. See feature/chat/CLAUDE.md, "A spec's preset becomes the chat's parameters".
entries.failure_mode: If upstream narrows or widens what gets unset, mobile's omissions change meaning: a value left out could start surviving (stale) or start being erased.

entries.why: Which Gemini models the server runs URL Context on (2.5+, not image/live/TTS/audio). The two regexes it reads are declared just above the function and are part of this mirror. The chat hides the toggle on other models (ChatUiState.urlContextProviderGate); web doesn't.
entries.failure_mode: The toggle shows on a model the server skips it for (a silent no-op), or hides on a newly supported one.

kotlin.symbol: the `bundle` entries (lucide-react, recharts, three, date-fns, react-router, dat-gui, shadcn-ui, vaul); exact pins in scripts/artifact-modules/package.json

entries.why: The npm packages web's Sandpack installs for every React artifact, i.e. what an artifact may `import` on web. The client vendors the same set as bundles (no CDN; see scripts/web-assets.json's `bundle` source type) and the runner reads them from the generated VendoredWebAssets.MODULES. Deliberate divergences, each explained in its registry entry: recharts and react-router-dom run AHEAD of web's pins (deprecated line / advisories); tailwindcss-animate is not bundled (a Tailwind plugin, not a module); three's addons and date-fns locales are not bundled. A package added here is one models can be told about and that fails on mobile with 'not bundled'. Reconcile through /update-web-assets: add the pin to package.json, a registry entry (or the shadcn-ui modules list), then --sync. Check the new version against the dependency policy, and give an unmaintained/deprecated/vulnerable one an `advisory` so users are asked before it loads.
entries.failure_mode: An artifact that renders on web shows 'This artifact imports "X", which is not bundled with the app' on mobile. A version bump on web (e.g. lucide-react's minor) means icons the prompt-era model writes may not exist in our pin, which fails as an undefined export.

entries.why: Which shadcn/ui components web mounts into every React artifact, at /components/ui/<key> (client sharedFiles spreads this map). The vendored shadcn-ui bundle registers each under that path; ReactArtifactImports aliases the artifact's import to it. build.mjs refuses to --sync while this list and the registry disagree, so a drift here is caught at the next re-vendor, but nothing forces a re-vendor; this entry does.
entries.failure_mode: A component web mounts is 'not bundled' on mobile; one web stopped mounting still renders on mobile (harmless, but no longer what the prompt describes).

entries.why: Where web mounts the shadcn sources: the literal mounts (/lib/utils) and the artifactUIComponents spread. The /components/ui/<key>.tsx template lives in uiComponentFiles, outside this block, so only build.mjs --sync sees a change to it. A new literal mount, or a moved or dropped spread, changes what an artifact can import without touching artifactUIComponents.
entries.failure_mode: An import path web serves is 'not bundled' on mobile, or mobile serves a component at a path web no longer mounts.

kotlin.symbol: shadcn-ui / vaul source.shadcn.components_url (pinned to an upstream commit)

entries.why: The shadcn/ui component SOURCES web compiles into each artifact (template literals in shadcnComponents). The vendored bundles compile the copy at the commit their components_url names, so a fix or restyle upstream does not reach mobile until those URLs (and the shadcn-ui entry's version) move to the new commit and --sync runs. Shares the file with the artifact-modes entry; a diff that only touches ArtifactModes is that entry's, not this one's.
entries.failure_mode: Components look or behave like the old upstream version: a styling fix, a new variant or a new export missing on mobile. Silent, since the old sources still compile.

kotlin.symbol: the `bundle` entries, and lucide-react's pinned version

entries.why: The server's artifact system prompt tells the model which libraries it may import ('The lucide-react@0.394.0 library is available', recharts, three, date-fns, react-day-picker, shadcn/ui at /components/ui/*). That list, not web's dependency map, is what models actually write against. Noisy (most edits are prose), but a changed library line or version is a direct signal: lucide-react is pinned to exactly the version this prompt names.
entries.failure_mode: The model is told about a library mobile doesn't bundle, or a version whose icon names differ from ours, and its artifacts fail on mobile only.

entries.why: The Tailwind build web's artifact iframes load. The client vendors the same pinned Play CDN build; a move to v4 (@tailwindcss/browser) renames utilities model output still uses, so follow it deliberately (see the tailwind entry's pin_reason).
entries.failure_mode: Artifacts style differently on web and mobile: utilities one build has and the other lacks.

entries.why: The code on the login 200, the refresh 200 and the authenticated-route 403 that say the account must set up 2FA before going on. The refresh store branches on it before reading the response cookies, and the response validator raises the setup gate on it.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames the code: a required-enrollment refresh reads as a malformed 2xx again (refresh limbo), the 403 raises nothing and every request fails with no way forward. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The 403 code a password sign-in of an identity-provider account gets while 2FA is enforced. LoginViewModel tells it apart from the email-login-disabled 403 so the form is not hidden.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames it and the sign-in screen tells an SSO user that email login is disabled on the server, and hides the form.

entries.why: The 403 code (flat {code}, or nested {error:{code}} on the remote agent routes; see packages/api/src/middleware/terms.ts) a write gets while the terms are required and not accepted. The validator raises the terms gate on it, which opens the Terms screen.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames the code or changes the envelope: every write fails with a generic error and the Terms screen never opens.

entries.why: The 403 code (and the OAuth callback error= value) a pre-auth route answers under strict tenant isolation when the request names no tenant. The sign-in and SSO screens give it their own explanation instead of 'email login disabled' or a generic failure.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames it and a tenant refusal reads as email login being disabled, which hides the sign-in form.

entries.why: Which configured policy links (privacy policy, terms of service externalUrl) may be opened: http(s), mailto, tel or relative, with the scheme read the way a URL parser reads it. Ported as a hand-written scan, not the regex.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream widens or narrows the allowlist and the client opens a link the web refuses (or hides one it shows). Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The account providers 2FA applies to (local, ldap). Account › Security offers 2FA only to them (web's isTwoFactorPolicyProvider), and Disable 2FA is hidden for them while twoFactorAuthenticationRequired is on, because only for them does the server refuse it.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds a provider: its accounts get no 2FA row, and Disable 2FA stays visible for it and fails with a 403 when tapped.

entries.why: One of the two cookies the MCP OAuth callback accepts as browser binding (v0.8.9-rc1). Mobile copies it by name from the bind response into the sign-in WebView's jar.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames the cookie: bind still answers 200 but the cookie is filtered out, the WebView carries no binding, and every in-app MCP sign-in ends at /oauth/error?error=csrf_validation_failed.

entries.why: The user-bound cookie the MCP OAuth callback accepts when the per-flow CSRF cookie is missing or was replaced by a later prompt.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames it: a sign-in whose CSRF cookie lapsed or was overwritten by another prompt fails with csrf_validation_failed instead of falling back to the session binding.

entries.why: The sign-in prompt's tool call is named oauth_mcp_<normalized server>; mobile reads the server name from it when the authorization URL's redirect_uri names no MCP callback.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the prefix: a prompt whose URL has no MCP redirect_uri shows no Sign in action, and the run waits until the prompt expires.

entries.why: The MCP OAuth callback ends with a redirect to {basePath}/oauth/success or {basePath}/oauth/error?error=; the in-app sign-in WebView stops on those two paths to report the outcome.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream moves the result pages: the WebView loads the web app's page and never reports success, so Settings does not reload and the user has to close the page by hand.

entries.why: What Read Aloud speaks: the TEXT parts of a reply (parseTextParts with skipReasoning), or its plain text minus a legacy :::thinking block. Reasoning is never spoken.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream widens or narrows what is spoken (a new part type, steer text, a different legacy split) and mobile keeps reading the old selection aloud; nothing fails.

entries.why: POST /api/files/speech/tts/manual synthesizes only the first speech.tts.maxInputChars characters (default 20,000) and drops the rest without an error. Server read-aloud sends a reply in segments well under it (SERVER_TTS_SEGMENT_CHARS), so a long reply is read to its end.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream lowers the default below the segment size: long replies read aloud through the server stop partway again, with no error.

entries.why: The sentence boundaries a long reply is cut at for read-aloud (server segments and the device engine's 4,000-char utterances), the same ones upstream's streamed speech splits on.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes its boundaries and mobile keeps cutting at the old ones; a segment may end mid-sentence where web's would not. Nothing fails.

entries.why: Which reasoning text is an encrypted provider payload (an unbroken base64/base64url run of 128+ chars, the persisted <think> wrapper ignored) and how a streaming tail is held until classified. The thinking card, find-in-page, copy and the editor's read-only rule all read it; an all-payload part renders the 'Reasoning (encrypted)' marker.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the threshold, the alphabet or the streaming hold, and mobile shows ciphertext as thinking again (or hides prose) with nothing failing.

entries.why: A chat POST the content filter refused is a 400 {error: 'content_filter_block', message, source, field}, nothing saved. The chat keys contentFilterNotice on that error id: the filter's sentence is shown, or a localized notice when it has none, never the bare code.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed error id makes a filtered send read as a generic 400; a body without a message then shows the raw code as the error.

entries.why: Every /api/agents/chat route 400s INVALID_MESSAGE_ID for a present turn id outside 1-256 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_:.-] (an empty string is present). ChatPayloadBuilder sends blank ids as absent, and ChatPayloadMessageIdTest pins mobile's ids against the rule.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream tightens the rule (new fields, a shorter limit, a narrower alphabet) and a send mobile builds starts failing with 400 INVALID_MESSAGE_ID while every test stays green.

entries.why: The attached-workspace bash_tool ends its output with an exit-status trailer ([exit code: N][terminated by SIG][timed out][output truncated]) written by formatCommandResult; the client reads it (as upstream Parts/command.ts parseCommandOutput does) to count a non-zero exit as a failed call in an activity-group header, and to split the code card into stdout, stderr and the exit badge ("Ran command · exit code 1"). The server serves no verdict field.
entries.failure_mode: The trailer's wording changes and every attached-workspace command reads as succeeded in the group header while its card (on web) shows the failure. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The server folds a digest node's children into a model-facing English tally ('bash_tool ×3, text +2 more', '1 turn, 2 tools'); the web client takes it apart with three regexes so every fragment but a tool name is localized, rebuilds the tree from positional paths ('3.2' under '3', '1-14' at the root) and opens the branch holding the active path. None of this is served as structure.
entries.failure_mode: The tally's wording or the path scheme changes and the progress card shows raw English fragments, or nests nodes under the wrong turn. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which stored graph edges the handoff editor owns: not edgeType 'direct', and not an untyped, unconditional edge from one source to several destinations, which the agents SDK runs as direct. The rule is the SDK's, copied by the web client; the server serves no classification.
entries.failure_mode: The SDK changes its default and the editor lists direct edges as handoffs (or hides real ones); an edit then rewrites the edge's meaning on save. Nothing errors.

kotlin.symbol: preparingToolLabel / MCP_DELIMITER / ACTION_DELIMITER; ActiveToolCall.isPreparing in viewmodel/MessagesState.kt

entries.why: When a live tool call reads 'Preparing {tool}': a preparation marker without a dispatch, result or terminal status (isToolCallPreparing; dispatch and results outrank the marker), and never for an MCP (`_mcp_`) or action (`_action_`, data-provider actionDelimiter) tool, which keeps its integration name. Upstream also reads incomplete arguments as preparing; this client tracks no argument deltas and does not.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the precedence or the integration exclusion and live cards say Preparing while a tool runs, or prefix a raw tool_mcp_server string. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The codes a failed audited permission update carries in its error body (permissionErrorCode), which the access editors word as 'try again' (busy lock, lock store down, audit log down) instead of a generic failure. Web maps the same set in client/src/components/Sharing/errors.ts.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds or renames a code and the editors fall back to the generic failure for a refusal that would pass on retry. Nothing errors.

kotlin.symbol: keepAcceptedInferenceParameters (profiles, ALIASES, parameterKey, knownFamily, Bedrock envelope hoist)

entries.why: Which model_parameters keys the v0.8.9-rc1+ agent create/update routes accept per provider family (openai, openrouter, anthropic, google, bedrock, bedrock-anthropic, mistral), how aliases map to profile keys, how a custom endpoint picks its family (defaultParamsEndpoint) and admits declared extras, and how a legacy Bedrock additionalModelRequestFields envelope is read. The editor drops every other key before saving, because the route rejects the whole save with a 400 otherwise.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream admits a new key and the editor deletes it from every agent it saves; or it stops admitting one and every save of an agent holding it fails with a 400 the user can't clear from mobile.

entries.why: The rename handler's named refusals: 409 conversation_title_ownership_not_ready while interface.runningChatRename is off and the title is unset or a run is active, and 404 conversation_not_found. The chat and the drawer word each instead of a generic failure.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames a code or adds a refusal and the rename falls back to 'Failed to rename conversation' with no hint that waiting would help. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The capability version /api/config announces when the server owns a running chat's title. StartupConfig.supportsConversationTitleOwnership compares the served number to this copy, so the copy is the half that is never served. Nothing reads that property yet (the rename refusals come from the server, see conversation-rename-refusals); it is registered so the first caller does not inherit a stale copy.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream bumps the version and supportsConversationTitleOwnership reads every new server as lacking title ownership. Inert until something reads it; then it silently withholds whatever that caller gates.

entries.why: Title ownership needs BOTH the announced version and interface.runningChatRename; a replica with the YAML option but no announced version is an older server.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds or drops a condition and the property answers wrongly for some servers. Inert until something reads it (see conversation-title-ownership-version).

entries.why: Which interface.retentionMode makes the server save every new chat temporary (only 'ephemeral'). The client locks the temporary toggle on, latches the flag on the created chat and keeps such chats out of the cache from it.
entries.failure_mode: Another mode starts forcing temporary chats and the client shows them as saved, caches them and offers a toggle the server ignores -- or the reverse, a toggle locked on for nothing.

entries.why: The literal behind RetentionMode.EPHEMERAL, which forced-temporary-retention's predicate names by symbol, so a renamed value would not move that block.
entries.failure_mode: The value is renamed and the client never recognises forced retention: every chat looks saved while the server expires it.

entries.why: How long a transport-ambiguous queued turn is reconciled when interface.queuedTurnReconciliationTimeoutMs is absent or invalid. The server serves the configured value, never its default.
entries.failure_mode: The default moves and the client gives up reconciling earlier or later than web, re-queuing a turn the server committed (a duplicate) or polling long after web has stopped.

entries.why: How long "Interrupt now" waits for /chat/steer/arm before saying it couldn't confirm, when interface.steerArmConfirmationTimeoutMs is absent or invalid. The server serves the configured value, never its default.
entries.failure_mode: The default moves and the client reports "couldn't confirm" sooner or later than web. No error either way.

entries.why: The error sentence the server writes into a tool an interrupt ("Interrupt and steer") cancelled. Module-private and served nowhere; the client matches it to draw the call as "Interrupted by your message" and count it as cancelled rather than failed.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream rewords the sentence and every interrupted tool goes back to reading as a red failed card, with its group header counting a failure. Nothing errors; the copy is simply wrong.

entries.why: The interface timeouts' validity bounds (positive integer, at most 2_147_483_647) the client applies before falling back to the default, and the landingHeading values ('entity' | 'greeting'). COARSE: the whole schema is one declaration, so expect it to report on unrelated interface options; diff the timeout and landingHeading arms.
entries.failure_mode: A bound or heading value changes and the client discards a configured timeout the server accepts, or keeps the entity title where web shows the greeting.

entries.why: Which prompt-group source is LibreChat's own. Any other source stores no text, so the client resolves it live and hides edit and delete, which the server refuses for it.
entries.failure_mode: The native value is renamed and every prompt reads as external (read-only, resolved on each open); a new external source is named as Langfuse, or its group shows edit controls the server refuses.

entries.why: A skill-file upload during a durable skill delete answers 409 { error: 'SKILL_DELETING' }. The client words it as the skill being deleted rather than an edit conflict.
entries.failure_mode: The code or status changes and the upload shows the bare code, or the editor reads it as another edit having landed first and offers a retry that can never succeed.

entries.why: The skill-file delete's half of skill-deleting-upload: the same 409 { error: 'SKILL_DELETING' } during a durable skill delete.
entries.failure_mode: As skill-deleting-upload, for deleting a file.

entries.why: The chat abort route's outcome codes on generation protocol v1, which mobile speaks: 409 RUN_STILL_ACTIVE and 409 ABORT_PERSISTENCE_FAILED (Retry-After, run kept) are retried; RUN_ALREADY_SETTLED is final. The route is an anonymous router callback with no declaration to anchor on, so the whole routes file is watched -- COARSE; diff the /chat/abort handler.
entries.failure_mode: A code is renamed or a new retryable outcome appears and Stop either gives up on a run the server kept for a retry (the partial is never saved) or retries one that already settled.

entries.why: Which statuses end the required-2FA setup flow (401 expired or retired setup token; 403 via isRetiredSetupFlow for policy or ban) and send the user back to sign in.
entries.failure_mode: A status moves and setup either retries a dead credential forever or throws the user back to sign-in on a recoverable error.

entries.why: The acknowledgement and finalization nonces are single-use: 400 once consumed, plus the 401/403 of a dead setup credential. These end the flow rather than retrying with the same nonce.
entries.failure_mode: A spent nonce is retried indefinitely (the user is stuck on the backup-codes step), or a transient failure ends a setup that could have finished.

entries.why: The 403 both setup predicates fold in by name, declared outside their blocks.
entries.failure_mode: As two-factor-setup-credential-dead.

entries.why: The lastSeenAt value the server stamps beside a real reply. The drawer's Finished group keys on it to tell a reply that finished unseen from a chat marked unread by hand.
entries.failure_mode: A changed watermark empties Finished: replies still show their dot, but nothing is lifted to the top. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: When a chat reads as unread: a reply stamp newer than the catch-up, a missing stamp reading as seen.
entries.failure_mode: The dot shows on chats the web shows as read, or the reverse; /seen is sent for chats already caught up, or never for one that is not.

entries.why: The endpoint-filter bounds the list route applies when a server does not publish conversationListLimits. The filter sheet stops a selection at them.
entries.failure_mode: The sheet lets the user pick more endpoints than the route accepts and the filtered list fails with a 400, or stops them short of what the server would take.

entries.why: The web's list-filter windows (Any time, Today, Previous 7/30 days, Previous year as 1/7/30/365 whole days back from local midnight) and which endpoints the filter offers (served names within maxEndpointNameLength, plus any still selected). The drawer's filter sheet copies them.
entries.failure_mode: The same filter lists different chats on the phone and the web, or the sheet offers an endpoint name the route refuses with a 400. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: Which approval modes the agent editor offers per MCP tool: upstream getToolApprovalConstraint's rule order (deny, ask, allow, then dontAsk/bypass) and its '*'-only glob over the agents toolApproval policy.
entries.failure_mode: The mode menu offers Always approve or a remembered mode the admin's policy will never honour (it saves and does nothing), or disables modes the policy allows. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: How a mode change is written to tool_options: a fresh approval_revision UUID on every change (or on a remembering mode without a valid one), inherit removing both fields while keeping the tool's other options.
entries.failure_mode: A changed mode keeps old grants alive (stale revision), or a remembering mode without a revision is silently ignored by the server. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: Which reasoning key and values a one-turn reasoningOverride may carry for an endpoint and model. The server runs the same function on the request, so the Thinking chip and the send-time check must agree with it.
entries.failure_mode: The chip offers a level the server refuses with an `Invalid reasoning override` SSE error frame on a 200 (the send fails), or hides itself for a model that takes one. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: Per-provider model rules for the reasoning key: Gemini budget vs level, adaptive vs manual Claude, the OpenAI reasoning-model regex, Azure needing a declared definition.
entries.failure_mode: Same as reasoning-setting-for-target, for one provider's models.

entries.why: The model-name patterns that decide whether an OpenAI, Claude or Gemini model takes a reasoning override at all (isKnownOpenAIReasoningModel, isManualClaudeThinkingModel, and the gemini-3+/gemma-4+ test).
entries.failure_mode: A new reasoning model gets no Thinking chip, or a non-reasoning one gets a chip whose sends 400. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: Which defaultParamsEndpoint values count as a reasoning capability for a custom endpoint.
entries.failure_mode: A custom endpoint backed by a newly listed provider gets no chip, or one that is no longer listed keeps a chip the server refuses.

entries.why: Only the reasoning keys of each parameter set (and that the set exists), which is what resolveReasoningSettingForTarget picks from. The registry's full lists are not used for this because they differ from upstream's (Bedrock Anthropic's effort key).
entries.failure_mode: The chip's key or level list disagrees with what the server resolves, so a send 400s or a level is missing.

entries.why: How OpenRouter's per-model catalog narrows reasoning_effort: Auto kept, unknown levels dropped, none dropped when mandatory, no efforts hides it.
entries.failure_mode: The sheet offers a level the provider refuses, or hides one it accepts.

entries.why: Which endpoints the client fetches GET /api/endpoints/reasoning-capabilities for (and hides efforts on until it answers).
entries.failure_mode: An OpenRouter endpoint offers its generic list unchecked (sends 400 for models without that effort), or a non-catalog endpoint waits forever for a catalog and shows no chip.

entries.why: The values each override key accepts (ReasoningEffort, AnthropicEffort, ThinkingLevel), used to drop declared options an override can never carry.
entries.failure_mode: A level upstream added is never offered, or one it removed is offered and 400s.

entries.why: Which Claude models take effort (adaptive) rather than a token budget, for the reasoning override key.
entries.failure_mode: A new Claude model resolves to thinkingBudget (chip hidden) or to effort where the server expects a budget (sends 400).

entries.why: Which Claude models that are not adaptive take a token budget (thinkingBudget) for the reasoning override.
entries.failure_mode: A manual-thinking Claude model resolves to no setting, or a non-thinking one to thinkingBudget; a replayed budget then 400s or is dropped. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The rename dialog's field stops at the length the server keeps (it truncates past it).
entries.failure_mode: Upstream raises the cap: names are cut short in the app for no reason. Lowers it: the server silently truncates a name the dialog accepted.

entries.why: Each code of POST /api/user/email/change gets its own string and lands under the field it concerns (email, password, or the dialog).
entries.failure_mode: A new or renamed code falls through to the generic 'request failed' message, and a field error stops highlighting its field. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The dialog refuses a current password over the schema's max(128) before sending, as it could never match.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream raises the cap: a long valid password is refused locally as incorrect and the user cannot change their email.

entries.why: After a 429 without Retry-After, Send stays off for the limiter's default window (EMAIL_CHANGE_USER_WINDOW, 2 minutes).
entries.failure_mode: A longer default window: the user retries early and each 429 logs another VERIFY_EMAIL_LIMIT violation toward a ban. Shorter: Send stays off longer than needed.

entries.why: An instructions save answered 409 with code CHAT_PROJECT_CONFLICT keeps the draft, reloads the project and offers View theirs; any other refusal is a plain save error.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames the code: a stale-revision save reads as a generic failure, the project is never reloaded, and every later Save conflicts again until the screen is reopened.

entries.why: On POST /:id/files a 409 (uncoded, { error }) is the project's file limit and is worded with the cap; a 400 is an ineligible file.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream gives the route another 409 meaning: it is told the project is full when it isn't.

entries.why: A project file row reads Ready only for availability 'ready'; anything else (including a new value) is Unavailable.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds a usable state (say 'processing'): the row reads Unavailable although the model can read it.

entries.why: The project editor caps the name where the server silently truncates it.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream lowers the cap: a saved name comes back shorter than typed. Raises it: names are refused locally that the server would keep.

entries.why: A project chat's start POST refused 409 PROJECT_RESOURCES_CHANGED, or 404 with the sentence 'Conversation context unavailable' (PROJECT_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE_MESSAGE; upstream CHAT_PROJECT_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE_RESPONSE above this block), gets its own copy instead of a generic failure.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream renames the code or rewords the 404: the send fails with a generic error that doesn't say the project changed or is gone.

entries.why: The text patterns that decide a failed reply reads as caused by its branch's files, which leads the recovery card with the cause sentence and offers Retry / Branch without files for failures that are otherwise unclassified.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds or rewords a pattern: a file-caused failure shows no recovery (or no cause sentence), or a non-file failure is blamed on the files.

entries.why: Typed failure codes that say nothing about their cause, so files may still be to blame and the recovery card is offered; any other typed code (a key, a balance, a limit) has its own remedy and hides it. Read through readErrorCode's envelope order, mirrored beside it.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds a code to the set: that failure shows no recovery here. Upstream removes one: recovery points at files for a failure with its own remedy.

entries.why: LangChain codes (read from the troubleshooting URL by parseLangChainErrorCode, packages/data-provider/src/langchain.ts, ported beside it) whose remedy is the model, key or rate limit, so no recovery is offered.
entries.failure_mode: A new remedial code is offered a pointless files recovery; a removed one hides recovery on a file-caused failure.

entries.why: Which turns count as carrying files (uploads, file-backed attachments, file locators in content, a steer's files): decides whether Retry and Branch without files are offered, and whether a copy from an older server still has its files.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream adds a file locator shape: a branch carrying only that shape offers no recovery, and an older server's copy holding it is announced as clean.

entries.why: The marketplace `sort` values the list route accepts (v0.8.9-rc1), in menu order. The route drops an unknown value silently and answers in its own order.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed or removed mode is sent and ignored: the list comes back in the default order under a menu label that says otherwise. A new mode is never offered. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The 409 `{ error: "cursor_ordering_mismatch" }` a cursor read under another order gets. The marketplace restarts the list from page one once per query on it.
entries.failure_mode: A changed status or body makes every such page read as an ordinary failure: the footer shows Couldn't load more and Retry repeats the same stale cursor.

entries.why: The consent view's `state` values, each worded in the sheet, and `expiresAtMs` in epoch milliseconds.
entries.failure_mode: A new state reads as Authorization required; a renamed one shows the wrong status. A change of the expiry's unit renders a deadline decades off. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: The `credentialMode` enum, each value labelled in the consent sheet's target card.
entries.failure_mode: A new mode shows as its raw wire value; a renamed one loses its label. The user authorizes without a readable description of how the server signs in.

entries.why: The strict confirm body: `expectedRevision` is nullable but required, and `lifetimeHours` is 1..8760. Built as a JsonObject so the null survives `explicitNulls = false`.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed or added required key makes every Confirm a 400 `consent_invalid`, shown as Authorization could not be updated.

entries.why: The server routes each agent to a machine with these exact rules (owner, then inherited parent, then default, then a single legacy pick) and validates a decision's ids, checkout and owners the same way. The composer resolves the same rules to know which workspaces a send must carry. Spec tables ported in CodeWorkspaceSelectionTest / CodeWorkspaceInheritanceTest.
entries.failure_mode: A changed precedence or validation makes the composer ask for a workspace the server never uses, or send a decision the server refuses as code_workspace_unavailable (invalid/required/locked). Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: Each /api/config capability version is matched with ==, as web does. The decision version is what allows sending a selection-less ("No workspace") decision; inheritance lets a subagent skip its own workspace.
entries.failure_mode: A bumped version reads as unsupported: the composer stops offering No workspace and holds sends, or asks subagents for workspaces they no longer need. Silent.

entries.why: When the workspace control applies, the per-machine state, the pre-selection order (agent default, remembered pick, sole workspace) and what a send carries (resolveSubmission). Two deliberate divergences are documented on the object.
entries.failure_mode: A changed rule pre-selects a different workspace than web, or sends a decision web would not, and the chat is sealed on it for good.

entries.why: Which agents a chat reaches (agent_ids, edges, enabled subagents and their graphs) and which machine each runs on, including per-chat machine choice from an agent's allowlist.
entries.failure_mode: An agent the composer no longer counts gets no workspace and the server refuses the turn as required, or a machine choice is offered that the server refuses.

entries.why: How a pick rewrites the draft decision: which machines it replaces, which fixed machines it keeps, and which agents own a per-chat machine choice (agentIds).
entries.failure_mode: A draft that keeps a replaced machine or drops an owner is refused by the server as invalid/required on the first turn.

entries.why: The six reasons a code_workspace_unavailable rejection carries; each has its own copy (error_code_workspace_*), from translation.json com_error_code_workspace_*.
entries.failure_mode: A new reason falls back to the generic message; a renamed one shows the wrong advice.

entries.why: Remembered workspace picks: keyed per server, user, agent and machine, most recent first, capped at 100.
entries.failure_mode: A different key or cap changes which workspace a new chat pre-selects.

entries.why: The query parameter that opts a message load (and fork, duplicate, shared fork, branch) into tool-call previews.
entries.failure_mode: A renamed parameter is ignored by the server: loads silently go back to full payloads.

entries.why: The preview format we understand; the server honours only an exact match.
entries.failure_mode: A bumped format makes the server send us full payloads again: safe, but the load-size gain is gone without notice.

entries.why: Keys a fetched full part to the stored version its preview stands for (previewRevision + FNV-1a of output, args and the three lengths).
entries.failure_mode: A key that ignores a changed field shows a stale fetched part after the stored call changed.

entries.why: Which flags make a call a preview; drives fetching, copy, export and the import refusal.
entries.failure_mode: A new marker flag goes unseen: a shortened call is copied, exported or shown as if it were full.

entries.why: Which fields a fetched full part replaces (only the shortened ones) and which markers it clears.
entries.failure_mode: A new shortened field keeps its preview after the fetch, or a fetched copy rolls back a newer cached field.

entries.why: The context gauge's estimate counts a preview at its full argsLength/outputLength (ContextGaugeResolver).
entries.failure_mode: The gauge drops sharply on every previewed chat.

entries.why: Which ui_resources entries are MCP Apps (get an Open app row) rather than legacy MCP-UI HTML.
entries.failure_mode: Apps the server attaches show no row, or legacy HTML is run through the App bridge.

entries.why: The CSP sources an App's declaration may contribute to its sandbox and its link allowlist.
entries.failure_mode: An App runs under a wider or narrower policy than web gives it, or opens links web refuses.

entries.why: The source grammar an App's CSP entries must match to be kept.
entries.failure_mode: Raw CSP syntax reaches the policy, or valid sources are dropped.

entries.why: The relay page's and the View's Content-Security-Policy, built natively because the app does not load /api/mcp/sandbox.
entries.failure_mode: An App gets egress, frames or scripts that web's sandbox denies.

entries.why: Which ui/open-link URLs the host opens: only hosts the delivered CSP declared.
entries.failure_mode: An App exfiltrates proxied MCP data through a host-opened link, or a declared link is refused.

entries.why: CSP3 host-source matching for links (scheme, port, wildcard, address literals).
entries.failure_mode: Link matching drifts from web's, widening what an App may open.

entries.why: The host-source grammar the link check matches against.
entries.failure_mode: Link matching drifts from web's.

entries.why: Bounds on an App's reported size (McpAppHost.reportedHeight); the inline slot's floor and ceiling (McpAppSessionRules) reuse them.
entries.failure_mode: An App reports a size the host trusts without bound.

entries.why: The tool-result notification an App receives after initialize.
entries.failure_mode: Apps that hydrate from structuredContent or _meta render empty.

entries.why: Which attachments become App rows, their identity key and ordinal.
entries.failure_mode: Rows duplicate or collide when a provider reuses tool-call ids.

entries.why: Which resources/read item is the App document and where its CSP comes from.
entries.failure_mode: A URI-only App loads the wrong document or runs under the default policy.

entries.why: When a server's mcpApps policy counts as enabled and which limits apply.
entries.failure_mode: Rows show on a server whose policy web treats as off, or limits differ from web's.

entries.why: The relay page is a port of the sandbox proxy's inner-frame half: sandbox token allowlist, View CSP meta + nonce heartbeat injection, head injection point, source and attestation checks.
entries.failure_mode: An App frame gains a capability or a message path web's sandbox refuses, or a new handshake step never reaches the App and every open times out.

entries.why: The host's capabilities, initialize/host context, tool-input-then-result order, what needs approval, the preview-size fail-closed rule and the message overrides.
entries.failure_mode: The Kotlin host advertises or allows something web's bridge does not, or an App waiting for a step web sends never gets it.

entries.why: The approval queue bound, cancel-pauses-the-View rule and stop-requests behaviour.
entries.failure_mode: An App can queue more actions, or keep asking after the user cancelled.

entries.why: Which spec style variables the host sends an App in its host context (mapped onto Material roles here).
entries.failure_mode: Apps theme a different subset than on web, or miss a variable web starts sending.

entries.why: Which declared App permissions reach the opaque App frame's `allow` attribute: geolocation and clipboardWrite only. The relay page's own `allow` port is covered by mcp-app-sandbox-relay; this is the filter native applies before sending `permissions` in sandbox-resource-ready.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream delegates a new capability (or drops one) and mobile Apps silently keep the old set: a feature that works on web fails the App's feature detection here, or one web withdrew is still granted. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The server tells the model to write `\ui{id}` / `\ui{a,b}` into its reply; the marker grammar (UI_RESOURCE_PATTERN), that it is matched only in markdown text nodes (never code), and single-id vs carousel are client-side rules the server never serves.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the marker syntax or the id alphabet and mobile replies show raw `\ui{…}` text (or swallow text web shows). Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which UI resources a marker may render: HTML media type (an omitted type counts as text/html) that is not the MCP App profile, and only while legacyHtmlEnabled.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream widens or narrows the renderable set and mobile draws resources web refuses, or leaves out ones web draws. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The legacy convention that a missing mimeType means inline HTML, and how a media type is compared (case-insensitive, parameters ignored). isHtmlMediaType sits in the same file and is watched through it.
entries.failure_mode: A resource web renders is skipped on mobile, or the reverse. Nothing errors.

entries.why: Markers resolve against every ui_resources entry in the conversation by resourceId, later ones winning, so a reply can place a resource from an earlier turn.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream scopes resolution differently (per message, first wins) and a marker resolves to a different resource than web's, or to none. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The chat message a legacy resource's tool / intent / prompt action becomes, worded for the model, and which action types are ignored (link, notify). Mobile asks before sending (web sends at once).
entries.failure_mode: Upstream rewords the message or handles another action type and the model gets different instructions from mobile than from web. Nothing errors.

entries.why: A multi-id marker is a horizontal carousel of 230x360 cards; one supported resource in it renders alone; none renders nothing.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the carousel's sizing or single-item rule and mobile lays resources out differently. Nothing errors.

entries.why: A single \ui{id} the conversation doesn't hold shows com_ui_ui_resource_not_found, checked before the legacyHtmlEnabled gate; a known but unsupported resource draws nothing.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream drops or rewords the chip, or moves it behind the policy gate, and mobile shows a chip web doesn't (or the reverse). Nothing errors.

entries.why: At most maxActiveViews Apps open (mobile also caps at 3, 1 on low-RAM); opening another is refused with com_ui_mcp_app_at_capacity rather than closing one.
entries.failure_mode: Upstream changes the cap or starts closing the oldest App, and mobile refuses where web opens (or the reverse). Nothing errors.

entries.why: Which chats may have a pull request: only those are ever asked, on the chat screen and in the drawer.
entries.failure_mode: Code chats show no pull request, or ordinary chats cost lookups.

entries.why: State/checks/provider to glyph, tone, CI dot and labels for the overflow item, sheet and drawer mark.
entries.failure_mode: The phone colours or words a pull request differently from web (e.g. a dot on a merged PR).

entries.why: Chat-screen polling cadence (20 s active, 60 s settled, stop when finished) and the 15 s / 60 s stale times.
entries.failure_mode: The chat polls GitHub through the server faster than web, or stops while checks still run.

entries.why: Batch chunk size (50) and PULL_REQUEST_BATCH_VERSION (1) the drawer gates its batch on.
entries.failure_mode: The server 400s an oversized batch, or the drawer asks a replica whose batch version it does not speak.

entries.why: When Settings shows the pull request account row: a grant to remove, or an app to connect whose status hasn't said it is gone.
entries.failure_mode: A stale grant can't be removed from the phone, or the row offers a connect the server refuses.

entries.why: Which status changes count as a change of credential (connect, disconnect, a new grant) and so re-ask every cached lookup.
entries.failure_mode: Pull request marks and the chat's PR stay as the old token saw them after connecting, or are re-asked on every status read.

entries.why: The provider names the account row and sign-in title use, the ones the server's success page names.
entries.failure_mode: A new provider shows as GitHub.

entries.why: The lookup failure codes the client logs; all read the same to the user.
entries.failure_mode: A new code is logged unnamed; behaviour is unchanged.

entries.why: A saved chat's move/attach/detach/recover: which machines a transition targets, how a target's pick inherits the replaced checkout and carries its owners' agentIds, when Confirm is ready, and which label and explanation (describeTransition) the change gets.
entries.failure_mode: A transition the server refuses as invalid/locked, or one whose label says Attach for a Move. Nothing fails to decode.

entries.why: Which failed turns re-read the chat's recorded decision before the next send (getFailedCodeDecisionRequest), and which approval mode a turn carries (resolveSubmittedCodeApprovalMode: ask without a workspace).
entries.failure_mode: A send after a failed first turn goes out without a decision and seals the chat, or a turn carries a mode web would not send.

entries.why: The three approval modes and which a machine's permissions allow (a mode needing allow needs the machine to offer allow and not deny it).
entries.failure_mode: The picker offers a mode the server refuses (CODE_APPROVAL_MODE_NOT_ALLOWED) or hides one it would accept.

entries.why: When the approval-mode picker shows (approvals on, ask offered, an attached machine in reach), the modes it intersects across machines, and the fallback to ask. The requested mode's order (conversation's, i.e. a spec preset's on a new chat, then the remembered pick) is CodeWorkspaceDelegate's requestedApprovalMode.
entries.failure_mode: The chip shows on chats where web hides it, or offers Full access on a graph web restricts.

entries.why: A turn carrying codeApprovalMode, ask included, is posted to queued-turns/v2; v1 409s it, and a turn queued without it runs under the attached machine's own permissions.
entries.failure_mode: If the routing rule changes, queued follow-ups either 409 or run edits and commands without the approval the chat asks for.

entries.why: The one-time command Settings shows after pairing: the pair and run invocations, their flags and the shell quoting.
entries.failure_mode: A user copies a command the current worker no longer understands; pairing fails on their machine with no hint from the app.

entries.why: The workspace scopes (user, agent-user, conversation), their UI order, and the fallback to the first allowed one, used by Settings' default and the agent editor.
entries.failure_mode: A new or renamed scope is not offered, or a preference the server refuses (400/403) is sent.

entries.why: A setup link's attempt id is 43 base64url characters; the paste field and librechat://code-setup links accept only that.
entries.failure_mode: A valid link is refused as not a setup link, or a malformed id reaches the server (404).

entries.why: The pairing route's 409s carry no code; only this message tells the machine limit apart from the other refusals.
entries.failure_mode: A reworded message shows the generic pairing error instead of telling the user to remove a machine.

entries.why: The editor blocks Save on a Git identity the server would refuse: both blank, or a 1-128 character name and a valid email (GitHub bot addresses included).
entries.failure_mode: Save fails with a server 400 the editor can't place, or a valid identity is refused locally.

entries.why: A user message taller than this (256, scaled with the chat font size) renders clamped with Show more, as web's collapseLongUserMessages does.
entries.failure_mode: Messages collapse at a different height than on web, or not at all.

entries.why: How far past the clamp height a message may run before the Show more toggle appears.
entries.failure_mode: A message that barely overflows gets a pointless toggle, or a clipped one gets none.

entries.why: The box (1900 x 1900) and quality (0.92) an image is resized to when the admin's clientImageResize leaves them out.
entries.failure_mode: Uploads are resized to a different size than web's for the same server.

entries.why: An admin-provided clientImageResize.enabled overrides the user's setting (enforced); sizes alone do not.
entries.failure_mode: An admin who forced resizing is ignored, or the user's switch is locked when it shouldn't be.

entries.why: Only these image formats are resized before upload.
entries.failure_mode: A format web resizes is uploaded full size, or one web leaves alone (GIF) is resized.

entries.why: Which bookmarks the drawer filter sheet offers: those some chat carries, plus every picked one.
entries.failure_mode: The sheet offers bookmarks that filter to nothing, or hides a picked one so it can't be turned off.

entries.why: Files per subagent-calls request; the route answers 400 past it.
entries.failure_mode: A message with many late files gets a 400 and its files stay where slice 1 guessed.

entries.why: How a paused server code tool (source librechat_code) reads in the approval review: which name and args make it a command, a create or an edit, the two hidden-character sets spelled out as \uXXXX (bodies keep tab/LF/CR, labels reveal them), and the per-call, per-label and per-batch caps with their order. The whole file is the rule, so it is watched file-level.
entries.failure_mode: A proposal reads differently on the phone than on the web: a bidi override or line break upstream started revealing stays hidden in a command or file name the user approves, or a cap drifts so a long proposal truncates elsewhere. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The review heading per preview kind (Run command, Create/Edit <path> or the generic variant, else the tool name) and the KIND_LABELS subtitle beside it.
entries.failure_mode: A heading upstream changed keeps the old wording or a kind gains a title the phone never shows.

entries.why: Which highlighter language a read or created file gets from its name and extension; FILENAME_MAP and langFromPath sit right after LANG_MAP in the same file.
entries.failure_mode: A file type upstream added renders as plain text on the phone. Cosmetic, silent.

entries.why: What a create_file/edit_file card shows: when the output counts as a diff (hasDiff), the 'Updated ' overwrite rule, the edits/old_text/new_text arg shapes, which pane supersedes which, and when the raw output is repeated below. The rules are spread across the component, so it is watched file-level.
entries.failure_mode: A create that overwrote a file reads as Created, an edit's diff is drawn twice or not at all, or a new arg shape shows an empty card. Nothing errors.

entries.why: How a tool's unified diff becomes rows (file headers only before the first hunk, line numbers from hunk headers, a bare @@ resetting them) and how an edit's args become a preview diff without a text round trip.
entries.failure_mode: A diff upstream learned to read differently miscounts additions, mislabels a changed line as a header, or numbers lines wrong.

entries.why: Reading a string field out of tool-call args that may be partial JSON: the field regex, the escape set, and the stream-edge hold-backs (dangling backslash, partial \u, split surrogate).
entries.failure_mode: A cut snapshot's file path or edit text shows escape debris or loses its tail.

entries.why: The user-readable names native tools get in the PTC trace and as a file card's fallback title. The Kotlin side splits MCP ids at the last _mcp_ without a server list.
entries.failure_mode: A native tool upstream named shows its raw id.

entries.why: How on_ptc_tool_call envelopes become a trace: append on running, update by call_id, drop a settle without its row, the 100-row cap with a dropped count. prunePtcTraces (running -> interrupted on resume) is in the same file, and PTC_TRACE_MAX_ENTRIES in hooks/SSE/ptc.ts.
entries.failure_mode: Rows duplicate, reorder or spin forever after a reconnect; the cap drifts. Nothing errors.

entries.why: The trace line's glyph per status and what a row shows (server · tool, args, duration or 'running', the failure under it).
entries.failure_mode: A status upstream adds renders without a glyph, or the line drops a field web shows.

entries.why: An attached command's trailer is shown dimmed, except after a timeout where it hides behind Details under the time-limit note; the verdict wording (exit code / terminated / timed out) is in the same component.
entries.failure_mode: A timed-out command's trailer shows or hides differently from the web, or a new verdict is never named.

entries.why: How the attached-workspace bash_tool's output splits into stdout, stderr and the [exit code][terminated by][timed out][output truncated] trailer. COMMAND_RESULT_TRAILER itself lives in packages/data-provider/src/previews.ts.
entries.failure_mode: A command's failure reads as success, or its trailer is drawn as stdout.

entries.why: Which fence languages get a Run button and what `lang` the execute_code call sends for each spelling.
entries.failure_mode: A language web runs shows no Run button here, or a run sends a lang the tool rejects.
