entries.why: Which fences take a block index (not math, mermaid or single-line) and the `${messageId}_${partIndex ?? 0}_${blockIndex ?? 0}_${toolId}` key (client/src/utils/map.ts mapToolCalls) stored runs are matched by.
entries.failure_mode: A run's output shows under a different block than on web, or a block's stored runs never show.

entries.why: Every colour role a server theme may name. A role missing here is dropped from the server's theme as unknown. Generated: rerun scripts/generate-theme-palettes.py, which fails on a token it cannot place.
entries.failure_mode: A role upstream added is ignored: the app paints the stock value where the server's theme names its own.

entries.why: Role names a release shipped and a later one renamed; a theme written with the old name keeps its value. Generated: rerun scripts/generate-theme-palettes.py, which fails on a token it cannot place.
entries.failure_mode: A theme naming a role by its old name loses that colour.

entries.why: The stock light palette every server theme is laid over. Generated: rerun scripts/generate-theme-palettes.py, which fails on a token it cannot place.
entries.failure_mode: Roles a server theme leaves out paint an old stock colour that the web no longer shows.

entries.why: The stock dark palette every server theme is laid over. Generated: rerun scripts/generate-theme-palettes.py, which fails on a token it cannot place.
entries.failure_mode: Roles a server theme leaves out paint an old stock colour that the web no longer shows.

entries.why: The bundled `clickhouse` theme lives in the web client, never on the wire: a server naming it sends only the name. Watches the whole file, since the light and dark maps and `clickHouseShape` (the corners and fonts the app reads) are all here. Generated: rerun scripts/generate-theme-palettes.py, which fails on a token it cannot place.
entries.failure_mode: A server on `theme: clickhouse` paints an outdated ClickHouse palette.

entries.why: Which corner or font a theme leaves out follows a broader one it names (composerActionRadius from roundControlRadius, displayFontFamily from fontFamily). Only the pairs for settings the app reads are copied.
entries.failure_mode: A theme that names only the broad setting reshapes the web's element but not the app's, or the reverse.

entries.why: The plain length forms a theme's corner settings may use (px, rem, em; calc() is theme-appearance-length-calc). A form the app can't read is left out, so that corner keeps Switchboard's.
entries.failure_mode: A corner written in a new form shows Switchboard's shape where the web rounds it.

entries.why: The calc() form of a corner length, which upstream keeps in its own pattern beside cssLengthPattern.
entries.failure_mode: A corner written in a new calc() form shows Switchboard's shape where the web rounds it.

entries.why: Which corner setting each element takes follows the class the web rounds it with (rounded-theme-surface-lg for the composer, rounded-xl for code blocks, .popover-ui for menus...). A renamed or remapped class here is the first sign an element moved to another setting; each ThemeShapes field names the class it follows.
entries.failure_mode: An element follows a different corner setting on the web than in the app; nothing errors.

entries.why: The names `interface.theme` may give instead of a definition. Each needs its palette mirrored (only `clickhouse` has one; `librechat` is the stock palette).
entries.failure_mode: A new bundled name reads as Invalid and the server's theme is ignored.

entries.why: Which inline definitions the client paints and which it ignores: fields, version, modes, colour token names and values. Appearance and brand values are checked for shape only.
entries.failure_mode: The app ignores a theme the web paints (it shows Switchboard's own look instead), or paints one the web ignores.

entries.why: The "R G B" colour format of every theme role.
entries.failure_mode: A theme in a new colour format reads as Invalid and is ignored.
